senses: Confused or puzzled.
ety: Blend of confused + puzzled. The earliest recorded usage is dated 1994, but the term was popularized in the early-to-mid-2000s.

senses: Marked with a stigma, or with something reproachful to character; stigmatized.
Impressing with infamy or reproach.
A plant formerly used to provide alkaline ashes for soap-making, Salsola aphylla.
An upward trend, or an upturn.
A circular gong that was struck at regular intervals to indicate the time.
The time interval indicated by striking the gurry. Originally, this was twenty-two and a half minutes, but later, under British influence, changed to an hour.
A small fort.
examples: Half a gurry after that, I went away too.
Since then, and in the course of yesterday afternoon, the town and gurry of Jubbulpore have been entirely evacuated by armed people of every description.

This was without the village, which, independently of the clay-built wall with which it was encircled, is further protected by a gurry, or little fort, on the acclivity of the hill, which arises from it to the westward.

senses: The art of using one or more turntables and mixers to create an original musical piece.
A cosmetic product that adds volume to the hair.
To tickle, to touch lightly.
ety: From Middle English kitelen, from Old English citelian (“to tickle”), from Proto-West Germanic *kitilōn, from Proto-Germanic *kitilōną, frequentative form of Proto-Germanic *kitōną (“to tickle”), from Proto-Indo-European *geyd- (“to stick, jab, tickle”). Cognate with Dutch kittelen, kietelen (“to tickle”), Low German kettelen, ketelen (“to tickle”), German kitzeln (“to tickle”), Icelandic kitla (“to tickle”), Swedish kittla, kittsla, Danish kilde and perhaps Old Armenian կիծ- (kic-, “to sting, bite”), but note that many such words are sound-symbolic. Compare tickle.

senses: The private orchestra or band of a prince or church.
ety: From German Kapelle. Doublet of chapel.
examples: And for rehearsals of those, the musicians of the capelle are required to appear on his demand.

senses: A very large siluroid fish (Pylodictis olivaris) of the Mississippi valley; the goujon or mudcat.
ety: Variant of pasha, several forms or relatives of which start with /b-/, e.g. Arabic بَاشَا (bāšā).

senses: The act or result of contorting; the state of being contorted: the twisting of something, especially oneself.
A performance art involving the dramatic bending and flexing of the body, showcasing extreme physical flexibility.
Having some specific type of trunk.
Of a two-way radio system: using a control channel to automatically assign frequency channels to groups of user radios.
The anniversary of one's first blog post.
examples: Blog soon begat a whole new generation of techno-neologisms in the blogosphere, where bloggers compile blogrolls, celebrate blogiversaries and suffer from blogorrhea.
When it comes around again, write a post celebrating your blogiversary..

senses: A pale yellow cheese from Valle d'Aosta in Italy.
ety: From Italian fontina. The name likely originates from either the Fontin mountain pasture or the village of Fontinaz in the Aosta Valley, where the cheese is traditionally produced.

senses: The smallest administrative unit of Ethiopia, contained within a woreda.
One who is holding a captive or captives.
One who catches or has caught or captured something or someone.
ety: Borrowed from Late Latin captor, from Latin capiō. English usage began around 1688.

senses: Something (a document, book etc.) that has a specified number of pages.
One who makes up type into pages of a book; one who binds or sorts pages into a book.
ety: From page + -er (agent noun suffix) or + -er (measurement suffix) (sense 3).

senses: A Tibetan Buddhist monk or nun who holds a certain academic degree.
A device, curved stroke, or flourish formed with a pen, coming at the end of a book or chapter; a colophon. For example: ⸎, ۞.
ety: From the Latin corōnis, from the Ancient Greek κορωνίς (korōnís, “crasis coronis”, “editorial coronis”); cognate with the French coronis.

senses: A poem or mantra, especially one recited mentally as part of meditation or mindfulness practice.
ety: Transliteration of Sanskrit गाथा (gāthā). Doublet of Gatha.

senses: A pair of long-beaked forceps.
ety: First attested in the 1500s. Calque of Dutch craenhals; cognate with German Kranichhals and Middle Low German kraneshals, all likely derived from Latin geranium, from Ancient Greek γέρᾰνος (gérănos, “crane”). By surface analysis, crane + -s- + bill. The flowering plant is so called because of the lengthened appendage of the seed vessel.

senses: Outside the body.
Prejudice or bias against persons on the basis of their skin color or complexion, often among persons of the same racial identification.
A style of painting characterised by the use of intense color.
examples: Black America used to be, and perhaps still is, a pigmentocracy, which means that the social hierarchy is based largely on colorism.
This type of preferential colorism isn’t only found in the church aisles, it’s at family gatherings, on the dating scene, in the classroom, on the playground—it’s everywhere.
Colorism from your own people feels worse than racism – at the very least your own family and people should welcome you, no?

senses: Having a scale expressed in nanometers.
A piece of jewelry; a trinket.
A small intricate piece of metalwork.
Beginning and ending in a similar way.
The absolute; the condition as it existed before the creation of the world.
ety: From the Hanyu Pinyin romanization of Mandarin 太極／太极 (tàijí). Doublet of taegeuk.

senses: The electronic, synthesizer-based subgenre of new wave and darkwave music, in contrast to that based on guitars.
One of various large carnivals held before the beginning of Lent, especially in Latin America.
ety: From Spanish carnaval, Portuguese carnaval. Doublet of carnival.

senses: An assessment equal to a quarter of the revenue, levied by the Marathas from other Indian kingdoms as compensation for being exempted from plunder.
A stegosaurus.
examples: First felt both happy and sad at the sight of the old stegosaurus. She thought of the time Mother had first brought her this way. She had growled at the giant stego, albeit from a safe distance.

senses: Study or love of antiques.
Study or love of antiquity.
The position a word or phrase occupies within the meter.
ety: Borrowed from Latin sēdēs (“seat”). Doublet of see.

senses: In the shape of a worm.
Of or related to royalists or some royalist faction.
Of or characterized by royalism.
